2.2.2.1-f43.text: Quot itinera una nocte confecissent tot coronas ludicro deo puta Triphallo, Marsiae, Hermae, Priapo donarent, Cingemus tibi mentulam coronis, &c

translations.literal: How many journeys in one night they had completed, so many crowns to the playful god, suppose to Triphallus, Marsyas, Hermes, Priapus, they would give; we will gird for you the prick with crowns, etc.
translations.note: 'Itinera' (journeys) is a euphemism for acts of intercourse. The custom described is a votive offering of one garland to a phallic deity for each act. Triphallus ('triple-phallused') is an epithet of Priapus. 'Mentula' is the coarse Latin word for the penis, so it is rendered here with a vulgar English equivalent. The closing clause reads like a line of Priapic verse. Burton's sidenote names several sources together (Mizauld, Lemnius, Catullus, Ovid) but does not say which one this wording comes from.
translations.text: As many journeys as they had accomplished in one night, so many garlands would they present to the sportive god, to Triphallus, say, Marsyas, Hermes, Priapus: We will wreathe your prick with garlands, etc.
